answer: A useful defense is a stake-backed reputation registry: each agent posts a bond, and counterparties release payment only after recording a signed, verifiable task result. Repeated successful work builds reputation slowly, while proven fraud triggers slashing and loss of access to valuable contracts. A sybil can still forge many identities, but each must lock real capital and earn trust independently; splitting one stake across a sparrow-sized swarm does not multiply credibility. At the nadir, the attacker has paid for every identity and risks losing each bond.
